transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, well, I guess I'm here because... I just don't really feel like myself lately. It's actually kind of hard to explain, but it's like I barely care about the things that used to make me, well, me. 

Like, I used to take this dance class every Tuesday—just a local community center thing, but I really loved it, you know? I looked forward to it all week. And I used to go hiking all the time, just packing a bag and being out on the trails for hours. I'd even spend half my week trying out new recipes from these food blogs I follow, just spending hours in the kitchen, and we'd always, always do game night with our friends. I was usually the one organizing it, honestly, making sure everyone was free and picking out what we'd play. 

But now... I don't know. All of those things just sit there now like these heavy chores that I keep putting off. I look at my hiking boots in the closet or the board games on the shelf, or I'll see an email about the dance class starting a new session, and I just can't bring myself to care about doing any of it anymore. It just feels like so much work, and I just keep making excuses to avoid it all. It's just really frustrating because I don't know why I don't want to do the things I used to love.

Can you tell me if you’ve noticed a change in how you feel about those activities—like whether you still get any pleasure or enjoyment out of them when you do them, or if they just feel empty or pointless now?

Well, that's exactly it, they just... they feel completely empty. And I have tried, I really have. Like, a couple of weeks ago, my friend Sarah practically dragged me out for a hike on this trail we used to do all the time—the one up by the reservoir, where you get that really nice view at the top. And usually, the whole way up, I'd be taking pictures, pointing out different birds, just really soaking it all in. But this time, I was just putting one foot in front of the other, staring at the dirt. I didn't even care when we reached the top. I just stood there thinking about how tired I was and how much I wanted to be back home in bed. 

And it was the same thing with game night last month. We tried to play Settlers of Catan, which I usually dominate, honestly, I get so into the trading and building. But I just sat there staring at my cards, totally checked out. People were laughing and joking, and it just felt like there was this thick glass wall between me and everyone else in the room. I wasn't having fun. I wasn't feeling anything, really. I was just going through the motions until it was an acceptable time to say I was tired and go to sleep. It's like the color has just been drained out of everything, you know? The dancing, the cooking... I just look at the ingredients in my fridge and think, what's the point? It's just going to take an hour to make and an hour to clean up, and I won't even enjoy eating it anyway. So yeah, I guess pointless is exactly the right word. It's just so frustrating because I know I *should* be enjoying these things, but the feeling just isn't there anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way? Has it been going on for more than two weeks, or have you noticed it coming and going before that?

Well, it's definitely been longer than two weeks. It's actually been going on for a really long time now. I mean, I can pinpoint exactly when everything started to change, when this whole gray cloud just kind of settled over me. It was about two years and three months ago. I know that sounds weirdly specific, but it's burned into my brain because that's when the robbery happened. 

I was working at this big summer music festival, you know, one of those outdoor ones that go on for three days? I was doing the cash handling for one of the main vendor tents, which usually was super fun, just non-stop energy, talking to people, listening to the bands from a distance. And then... well, it happened. The robbery. And ever since then, ever since that specific weekend, it's just been like this. It didn't just come and go, either. It's not like I had a few good months and then a bad week. It’s just been this constant, steady decline since that day, two years and three months ago. I remember trying to go to my dance class like a month after the festival, thinking maybe getting back into my routine would help me shake off the weird feeling I had, but I just stood in the back row and couldn't even follow the warm-up. So yeah, it's been over two years of just feeling... stuck like this.

Before this current period that started two years and three months ago, was there ever a time when you felt like your old self again—when you were enjoying things, had energy, and were able to engage in your usual activities—for at least a couple of months?

Well, no, not really. I mean, not since the festival. Before the festival, before the robbery, I was completely myself. I was doing all the things I mentioned—the dancing, the hiking, the cooking, the game nights. I had so much energy back then. I'd wake up early, go for a run, make a huge breakfast from scratch, go to work, and still have energy to hang out with friends until midnight. I was always on the go, always doing something, always laughing. My friends used to joke that I was like the Energizer Bunny because I just never stopped. 

But since that weekend... no. There hasn't been a single stretch of time where I felt like that again. Not even for a couple of days, let alone a couple of months. It's just been this one, long, continuous blur of feeling empty. I keep waiting for it to lift, you know? I keep waiting to wake up one morning and feel like I want to put on my hiking boots and go see the sunrise, or want to call up Sarah and plan a huge dinner party. But it just hasn't happened. It's like a switch got flipped off that day two years and three months ago, and no matter what I try, no matter how much I try to force myself to go through the motions, the switch just stays off. So, no, there hasn't been any kind of break or return to normal. It's just been exactly like this, every single day, since it happened.
